name: TX-26
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent running with no outside opposition spending
model.rationale: Brandon Gill holds a Republican-leaning seat, has outraised his Democratic opponent by more than 200-to-1, and faces no outside spending against him. Prediction markets price his reelection near 98%, consistent with a likely-to-safe Republican win.
model.watch: Any late polling or a major outside-spending infusion into the district would be the first sign the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brandon Gill seeks a second term in a north Texas district that leans Republican by about eleven points. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised over $4 million while Democrat Steven Shook has raised under $20,000 and reports only a few thousand dollars on hand. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive.

With no public polling available, the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbency advantage, and the lopsided money gap. Prediction markets give Gill roughly a 98% chance of winning. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot. The race is rated Likely Republican, with a modest chance of an upset only if the political environment shifts sharply.
